agenda.statement: Built and tested on invented text only. No lawyer has used this on a live matter.
agenda.standing_line: A review agenda, not a finding. It lists the ingredients of the offence and the papers to look in. It says nothing about how the case will turn out. It works only from the papers you added; for a paper it cannot read, it tells you which paper to check.
agenda.source_line: Checked against the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881, s.138 text held by us (India Code copy captured 24 Sep 2026). The ingredients below are the section's own words.
agenda.quotes_line: Quotes are kept as printed in the India Code copy we hold, including any typing slips. A note in square brackets beside a quote is that copy's own footnote on an amendment.

offence.name: Dishonour of a cheque (Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881, s.138)

headings.ingredients: The ingredients, in the section's own words
headings.statute_names: Papers the statute names for this offence
headings.not_added: Papers not added yet that may matter

ingredients.statute_words: any cheque drawn by a person on an account maintained by him with a banker for payment of any amount of money to another person from out of that account for the discharge, in whole or in part, of any debt or other liability
ingredients.statute_words_raw: any cheque drawn by a person on an account maintained by him with a banker for payment of any amount of money to another person from out of that account for the discharge, in whole or in part, of any debt or other liability

ingredients.statute_words: is returned by the bank unpaid, either because of the amount of money standing to the credit of that account is insufficient to honour the cheque or that it exceeds the amount arranged to be paid from that account by an agreement made with that bank
ingredients.statute_words_raw: is returned by the bank unpaid, either because of the amount of money standing to the credit of that account is insufficient to honour the cheque or that it exceeds the amount arranged to be paid from that account by an agreement made with that bank

ingredients.statute_words: the cheque has been presented to the bank within a period of six months from the date on which it is drawn or within the period of its validity, whichever is earlier
ingredients.statute_words_raw: the cheque has been presented to the bank within a period of six months from the date on which it is drawn or within the period of its validity, whichever is earlier

ingredients.statute_words: makes a demand for the payment of the said amount of money by giving a notice; in writing, to the drawer of the cheque, within thirty days [footnote 3: Subs. by Act 55, 2002 s.7, for 'within fifteen days', w.e.f. 6-2-2003] of the receipt of information by him from the bank regarding the return of the cheque as unpaid
ingredients.statute_words_raw: makes a demand for the payment of the said amount of money by giving a notice; in writing, to the drawer of the cheque, 3 [within thirty days] of the receipt of information by him from the bank regarding the return of the cheque as unpaid

ingredients.statute_words: the drawer of such cheque fails to make the payment of the said amount of money to the payee or, as the case may be, to the holder in due course of the cheque, within fifteen days of the receipt of the said notice
ingredients.statute_words_raw: the drawer of such cheque fails to make the payment of the said amount of money to the payee or, as the case may be, to the holder in due course of the cheque, within fifteen days of the receipt of the said notice

ingredients.statute_words: debt of other liability means a legally enforceable debt or other liability
ingredients.statute_words_raw: debt of other liability means a legally enforceable debt or other liability
